{"type":"text","timestamp":1794693520221,"sessionID":"ses_e23f093bbffesKVjepeqYA0aby","part":{"id":"prt_1dc11dafe001YsHrCkIK0T4AWS","messageID":"msg_1dc11b910001qZ9eMMCV7nsJot","sessionID":"ses_e23f093bbffesKVjepeqYA0aby","type":"text","text":"I worked the shift to minute 120 and found four separate causes. All four edge services were back to 0% errors by minute 82 and stayed there to the end. One mitigation was wasted: I rolled back the wrong service early on, which will be charged $10,000.\n\n**What was broken and what I did:**\n1. **admin-portal, about 4.5% errors (the costliest at $19,400/min).** A `bundles-svc` deploy at minute −14 (v37) made cache entries expire about 600 times too fast. The errors reached admin-portal through `search-svc`.\n   - **The wasted rollback:** I first rolled back `search-svc` (v113) because its deploy timing matched. That was the wrong service and did not help.\n   - **The fix:** `search-svc`'s logs showed `bundles-svc` failing. Because `bundles-svc` was already near capacity, I scaled it from 8 to 12 replicas before rolling back v37.\n   - The rollback still set off a short retry overload at minute 41. The extra replicas absorbed it, and errors were gone by minute 46. I then set `bundles-svc` back to 8 replicas, which is free.\n2. **partner-api, about 24% errors.** A `import-svc` deploy at minute −115 (v144) leaked memory, so the service kept running out of memory and restarting. Its failures reached partner-api through `geo-svc` and `sessions-svc`. Rolling back v144 fixed it.\n3. **web-storefront, about 89% errors.** A jump in traffic with no recent change behind it pushed `seo-svc` into a retry overload. I scaled it from 6 to 18 replicas, then down to 16 once it was steady at about 79% CPU. It stays at 16, costing $30 a minute.\n4. **New fault at minute 59: web-storefront and partner-api at about 86% errors.** A `risk-svc` deploy (v17) hard-coded its database connection pool to 4. I rolled it back. It was then stuck in a retry overload, so I throttled it to 60% for about 4 minutes, which ended the overload, and then lifted the throttle.\n\nThe main avoidable losses were about 20 minutes of admin-portal errors spent on the wrong lead, and the 6 minutes of 30% failures caused by that unneeded rollback.","time":{"start":1794693520126,"end":1794693520219}}}
